source.original_title: 05/06/2026 - Nicholas Ugo & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/06/2026 - Nicholas Ugo & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Lost

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'You spoke with Kim, I think. He kind of left me some notes, so I have a background on you.' Prospect twice references the prior call — 'I did share that with Kim. I don't know if he put that in the notes' about losing his job, and 'I mentioned all that to Kim yesterday, in terms of the digestibility of the payment plans'.

prospect.name: Nicholas Ugo
prospect.location: Suburban Austin, Texas, USA — moved there from Chicago about five months earlier, via roughly eighteen months in Wisconsin. Has no vehicle.
prospect.occupation: Group facilitator — was working for a group he names as the Asbury group in Austin and was let go shortly before this call. Currently unemployed and part-way through a men's coaching certification with a business-building component; has no clients or business set up yet.
prospect.family_status: Refers to a 'dicey childhood'; no partner or dependants mentioned
prospect.training_background: Long-time calisthenics proponent; describes himself as an ectomorph. Best shape of his life about five years ago in Chicago at roughly 10-12% body fat, living near the lake with a gym in his building. Has plateaued on bodyweight work and is bored with it. Not new to kettlebells but not expert — has owned a 35 lb bell and used them in gyms, has written short kettlebell routines for himself. Was vegan at his peak and alcohol-free for four years; both lapsed during the Wisconsin period. Does not want to run and has no gym access in Austin.
prospect.medical: Self-describes a 'super, super mild S-curve in the mid-spine', volunteered only after the rep disclosed his own scoliosis, and states he has no pain or restriction: 'I don't function with any pain or any restriction. And I just like to keep it that way.' Sleep has degraded since losing his job — 'I don't fall asleep as quick as I as I used to' — with no history of insomnia. Reports confidence 'waning a little bit right now'.

signals: Two years of lost ground dated precisely: 'When I left Chicago is when I would consider the clock starting as far as the fall off'
Wants a former self back and can describe it exactly — 185 lb at single-digit body fat, versus 10-12% five years ago
Lost ground to a hard season rather than to choice: relocation, isolation in a suburb with no car, lapsed veganism and sobriety, then redundancy

Carries the regret openly, including about how he presents it: 'I think my ego doesn't want me to start with this, but it was the first thing that came to mind, so I'm just going to go with it, is the aesthetics'
Not price-resistant by disposition — genuinely without capacity: 'currently unemployed, coming out of pocket, don't have any credit to put it on, don't have anybody to borrow from'

goals.text: Get to 185 lb total body weight at single-digit body fat, from about 170 lb at 15-18%
Lose fat while adding muscle — 'I want to feel better than I look'
Get back the peak-health feeling — strong, energised, low brain fog, focused, spry
Break through a plateau and find challenge after years of calisthenics — 'I want to break through. I want to level up.'
Keep functioning without pain or restriction at 48
Rebuild consistency after two years of falling off
Explore nervous system and somatic work, which is what drew him to the coach in the first place

pains.text: Two years of decline in activity, consistency and muscle mass dating from leaving Chicago
Bored and plateaued with calisthenics, mentally and physically — 'I know that I can access it. I just don't want to, I'm bored and I don't want to do it by myself.'
Isolated in suburban Austin with no vehicle and no gym membership, five months after relocating for a job
Just made redundant from the job he relocated for, with no business, clients or income yet
Sleep has deteriorated since the job loss — takes longer to fall asleep
Confidence waning and hoping a fitness win will bleed into other areas
Overwhelmed by the volume of conflicting nutrition and training information available
Diet and four years of sobriety both lapsed during an eighteen-month period in Wisconsin; diet since corrected

objections.raw_quote: I know that it's not the most ideal, but I would be 100% coming out of, you know, currently unemployed, coming out of pocket, don't have any, don't have any credit to put it on, don't have anybody to borrow from, kind of thing. So I would, yeah, I would be paying for it myself.
objections.rep_response: Laid out three structures — full up front, 2 x $3,000 at 60 days (offering to stretch to 90), or $1,200 a month which he stated works out to more — then, on hearing there was no credit, raised a third-party finance option anyway and walked him through an application.

objections.raw_quote: even $1,200 right now, I don't have to, I don't have to part with. So, yeah... I think that the better move for me is to just focus on getting a job, and I like this 3K, 3K thing... but I gotta know that it's there.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it. No OD play ran. He then returned to financing — 'It's a shame, your credit's pretty chopped. Cause if your credit was pretty good, you can spread it over 12 months' — and ran a soft-pull application which was declined.

objections.raw_quote: I'm only imagining that you guys don't want the payments to go beyond the six months.
objections.rep_response: Confirmed the constraint implicitly and priced the alternatives, noting that monthly beyond the block costs more.

tiers.note: Monthly route at $1,200 per month — the rep stated it 'works out to be a bit more' than $6,000.

Third-party financed route: 12 payments of $650. Rep disclosed the headline — 'It will say 7800 in the top, but if you pay it off early, it reduces that load.' Application submitted on the call and declined.
Primal University, the self-guided product, offered as the fallback: '200 bucks a month. There's no commitment in terms of time frame... it's monthly rolling.'

offer.payment_plan_terms: Three routes named plus financing: full up front; $3,000 down and $3,000 at 60 days with an offer to extend to 90; $1,200 per month rolling, stated as costing more overall, with early payoff removing the $200 monthly premium; or 12 x $650 through a third-party lender totalling $7,800 before early-payoff reduction. The finance application was run live on a soft credit pull and returned 'we're sorry, we're unable to offer you a payment plan at this time'.

evidence: Prospect declined on capacity, not on desire: 'even $1,200 right now, I don't have to part with' and 'I think that the better move for me is to just focus on getting a job'
Third-party finance application submitted live and declined: 'we're sorry, we're unable to offer you a payment plan at this time'
Rep redirected to the $200/month self-guided product and sent the Skool link in the Zoom chat — 'I forgot what you, I always forget about. It's called Primal University'
No payment, no deposit, no onboarding call and no follow-up call booked; contact continues informally on WhatsApp

Counter-evidence for reading it as merely deferred: intent is genuinely high — 'this is something that I'm 100% dedicated to' — and the rep framed it as a pause: 'once you're in a better spot financially, we can kind of chat again'. What is lost is the $6,000 offer, which is what this corpus measures; the $200/month path stays open
outcome.next_step: Prospect to look at the Primal University Skool group at $200/month while focusing on finding work; rep to stay in touch on WhatsApp and revisit coaching when his finances recover.

notable.note: The prospect told the setter the day before that he had just been let go and that payment-plan digestibility was his issue — 'I did share that with Kim. I don't know if he put that in the notes' — and neither fact reached the closer, who spent 55 minutes selling a $6,000 programme to an unemployed man and then ran a credit application on him that was declined. The financed route he was walked through totals $7,800. This is also the second call in the batch, and the third mention of the product, where Primal University at roughly $200/month becomes the answer to a high-ticket affordability objection. The tax write-off pitch was started for the fifth time in the batch and correctly abandoned once the prospect said he has no business. Roughly the last eleven minutes of the call, after the sale was lost, are personal conversation about ancestry testing.

quality.notes: Severe and sustained. Speaker labels invert at almost every turn boundary in the second half — the entire Primal University pitch from 00:45:56 to 00:48:34 is attributed to the prospect when it is plainly the rep's, and the payment-structure explanation at 00:34:21 alternates mid-sentence. Long unpunctuated merged blocks at 00:10:00 to 00:11:03, 00:14:37 to 00:16:00 and 00:29:56 to 00:31:00. The rep's scoliosis disclosure at 00:14:00 is correctly labelled and consistent with three other calls in this batch; the prospect's mild S-curve disclosure at 00:14:37 is his own and is recorded as such. One fragment at 00:51:45 — 'let me quickly remove like um' — resembles the recording-stop phrasing used elsewhere in this batch, but the recording continues for a further four minutes, so no cut occurred.
